verdict.rationale: Zulip documents its own bot framework. Users can write a custom bot or run an existing one that reacts to messages, and deploy it on the Zulip Botserver so it stays up in the background. That gives event-driven automation, but it requires hosting and usually writing code, and the evidence shows no built-in automation builder, scheduling, or AI agent. Missing for 10: recurring/scheduled automations, a no-code or built-in automation setup, AI-native autonomous agent features, independent or hands-on corroboration of background bot operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Zulip’s API has a powerful framework for interactive bots that react to messages in Zulip. You can write and run a custom bot, or run an existing Zulip bot.
Eventually, you’ll probably want to run it in a production environment where it’ll stay up, by deploying it on a server using the Zulip Botserver.
